This is a nested donut chart displaying two concentric ring layers, each representing a distinct categorical variable with proportional segments. The outer ring, labeled “Ambiguity Std (Outer),” is divided into four segments corresponding to standard deviation values of 0.0, 0.47, 0.82, and 0.94, colored in descending shades of blue from dark to light; their respective proportions are 49.0%, 7.0%, 5.0%, and 47.7%, with percentage labels placed directly on each segment. The inner ring, labeled “Max Ambiguity (Inner),” consists of three segments representing maximum ambiguity values of 1, 2, and 3, colored in progressively lighter shades of blue; their proportions are 38.0%, 39.0%, and 14.2%, also labeled directly on the segments. A legend to the right of the chart provides color-keyed labels for both rings, with the outer ring’s legend using dark to light blue to indicate increasing standard deviation, and the inner ring’s legend using light to very light blue to indicate increasing maximum ambiguity. No segments are exploded or visually emphasized beyond their color and labeled percentage; the segments within each ring appear to be arranged in no consistent size order.
